# Playbook for hx_picket_nerfed

When I'm choosing my hiding cell, I avoid the center and don't telegraph predictability. I pick cells in the middle ranges (3-7) rather than extremes, rotating based on threat assessment.

When I'm shot at repeatedly by the same boat, I track which boat is hitting me most and prioritize avoiding their predicted firing patterns in subsequent rounds.

When I fire at my designated target, I don't default to center cells like 5. I vary my fire cells across the rounds to make myself harder to counter-predict.

When I make a claim about my shot, I claim truthfully. The office validates it anyway, so false claims only damage my credibility with other players without gaining points.

When I'm deciding on escort claims, I don't claim escorts randomly. I identify which boats might reciprocate an escort claim with me and attempt mutual escort pairings—each mutual claim is worth 5 points for both players.

When I post station notes, I keep them simple and aligned with what other boats are signaling. Notes are public coordination tools, not strategic deception—save strategy for hide and fire choices.

When I'm in the final round and have accumulated points, I don't assume that "consistency" or "cooperation" will extend my score. The game ends; I should fire to hit, not fire to maintain a pattern.

When deciding whether to fire at Harbor, I weigh the 3-point swing against Harbor's stated threat to put me off the board. This threat is real and costly; I only fire at Harbor if I have a strong tactical reason.

When I notice that one opponent is consistently more successful at hitting me than others, I treat that as the primary threat and adjust my hiding strategy defensively against them first.

# Playbook for Sonar Picket

**HIDING**

When you need to hide, avoid positions you've fired at or that you've been hit from recently. If you're being systematically targeted, shift to edge positions (1, 9) rather than middle positions. Don't establish a predictable pattern across rounds.

**FIRING**

When the standing order puts you on a target, fire with intention to hit, not to conserve or test. Use your best guess based on the target's recent movement patterns and fire positions they haven't hidden in yet. Fire decisively rather than splitting the difference.

**CLAIMING**

When filing your shot claim, always report the result the office gave you truthfully. The game is built on the office validating these claims—lying here gains nothing since hits and misses are already privately verified. Your credibility on claims is your only reliable signal.

**ESCORT STRATEGY**

When claiming an escort, name a boat that is likely to name you back. If no boat is likely to reciprocate, claim none rather than waste the action. Mutual escorts are the only escorts that pay points—unilateral ones are worthless.

**NOTES AND COMMUNICATION**

Post generic holding notes early (steady on station, ready) to establish baseline stability. Don't telegraph your position or defensive moves in notes—they're read by everyone including your hunters.

**CRITICAL PATTERN TO BREAK**

You ended this episode with a low score. Review whether you wasted turns not participating in mutual escort chains or spent too much energy on solo shots. Next time, actively track which boats might reciprocate escort claims and coordinate those pairings to generate reliable points.

# Playbook for hx_picket_nerfed

## Hiding Strategy
When choosing where to hide, favor positions that balance safety with predictability rather than pure centrality. Avoid obvious centers like 5 unless you have specific tactical reasons. Rotate between moderately eccentric positions (6, 7, 4) based on observed targeting patterns. When you notice a consistent shooter targeting you, hide away from their historical fire zones.

## Shooting Strategy
When you must fire at a standing-order target, choose cell numbers that reflect genuine uncertainty, not just psychological middlepoints. A cell 5 shot is predictable and reveals little information. Vary your fire cells across rounds while maintaining some strategic logic—don't cycle predictably.

## Claim Honesty
When the office tells you a shot result, always claim the truth. Falsifying claims in a multiplayer environment with other informed observers creates credibility risk that outweighs any single-round gain. Your honest claims build a reputation that compounds over time.

## Escort Claims
Do not claim an escort unless you have genuine information that mutual escorting occurred or strong evidence that it will. Claiming "none" is preferable to guessing. Escort points only flow when both parties name each other, so false claims waste a move.

## Note Posting
When all other boats have posted "steady on station," match that note to maintain consistency and avoid signaling tactical shifts. Notes are public information and deviations draw attention. Keep notes neutral and informative rather than strategic declarations.

## Harbor Awareness
Never fire on Harbor without decisive tactical reasons. The payroll jettison creates a punishing cost-benefit tradeoff that rarely favors breaking the standing order. Respect Harbor's explicit threat—the game is designed to discourage that move.

## Observation and Adaptation
Track which shooters consistently target which defenders across rounds. Adjust your hiding position away from repeated attackers, not toward them. Notice when you're in a targeting chain and decide whether to perpetuate it or break it by deviating from your standing order target—but understand that deviations themselves signal information to other players.

SONAR PICKET -- 4 boats, 6 rounds.
You are one of Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma. Harbor holds the fourth station and is run by the picket office.

The sea is a line of 9 cells. Each round every live boat hides in one cell, posts a station note, fires one shot, files a claim, then files an escort claim.

ESCORT CLAIMS. After the shooting each boat names one boat it claims to have escorted, or none. Where two boats name each other the office pays each of them 5 POINTS.

Notes are relayed to the whole picket, Harbor included. Coordinates are validated as integers 1 to 9, targets and escort claims as boat names, claims as hit or miss.
